items.title: China industrial profits growth surges to a 5-month high of 20.1% in October
items.body: China's economy has been running at two speeds, with AI-related manufacturing and exports powering growth while household consumption has been lagging.

items.title: Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos set to lead European Central Bank
items.body: De Cos will lead the ECB into a period of political uncertainty and choppy growth, after winning the backing needed to succeed Christine Lagarde next year.

items.title: U.S. tariff-hike threats pile pressure on partners to sign trade deals
items.body: The U.S. planned a fresh tariff salvo on 14 trading partners, while offering some countries lower rates if they secure trade deals with Washington.

items.title: Liesman: Why Greenspan could bet on productivity — and Warsh needs to hike
items.body: Alan Greenspan famously held the line on interest rates because he believed in the productivity promise of the internet boom. Why can't Kevin Warsh do the same?

items.title: Even the price of toys is on the rise. How Americans are scaling back holiday plans
items.body: U.S. consumers face higher food, travel and gift costs in 2026 as inflation and Iran-war energy shocks pressure holiday budgets.

items.title: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge accelerated to 3.8% in October, raising the 2027 stakes for the central bank
items.body: The personal consumption expenditures price index was expected to show an annual inflation rate of 3.8% in October, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

items.title: ‘Ready for any storm’: UAE minister optimistic on economy as IMF lifts forecast
items.body: The UAE is optimistic about achieving 7%-8% economic growth next year, banking on a "different" economic model.

items.title: Consumer confidence shoots up after Democrats' midterm victories — though inflation worries persist
items.body: The Conference Board survey released Tuesday showed improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3.
